## How to Destroy Angels - A Drowning (Drowned by Jaya Prime) \[[Free DL](https://sanjayaprime.bandcamp.com/track/a-drowning-drowned-by-jaya-prime)\]

There were a few years where one of the most tight-knit communities of DJs, remixers, and mashup artists all gathered on the (now defunct) Remix dot NIN dot Com. Some of us even met together to jam out, while even more of us continued collaborating during the heyday of SoundCloud. My friend Lita and I still do this day keep in touch despite having a decade passed since losing the site. Going into 2k10, RMX NIN and SoundCloud were cornerstones for a veritable "second renaissance" for independent music. To Trent Reznor and Atticus Ross of both NIN and HtDA, as well as Mariqueen Maandig of HtDA, so much love and gratitude for the many songs, stems, and inspiration by allowing all of us to experiment with your music. It can't. . really it can't be put into words how much that community and opportunity meant.

It's one thing to master your art, to fucking tear apart and create music the way you do. _Fucking legends!_ Then another thing entirely to open up your art to see what others make of it. That shit right there turns legends into myths that span lifetimes.

While I'm known for quite a few of my remixes and mashups from both bands, including the smash mashup "[The Making of a Violent Cyborg Heart](making-of-a-violent-cyborg-heart)", the remix that has spread the farthest and hit the most is easily my "drowned" remix of "A Drowning" itself. It was the first song I heard from the newly formed How to Destroy Angels and even the video was one you'd never forget. I've gotta include that here below: Strike that, that's.. . that's fucked up.

There's been a murder, so instead.. . yeah, I'm including the follow-up video for _"The Space in Between"_ instead.

texts: "What if everything around you isn't quite as it seems?"
\- Nine Inch Nails, Right Where It Belongs

But for anyone else who suffers from paradox syndrome and remembers...

* * *

\--- Click to Show More ---

* * *

It was rewritten... the video's gone, never even made in our current reality. "A Drowning" is the spiritual inheritor of "The Wretched" ([YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ANjQ8wI-W7g)) by Nine Inch Nails. It was HtDA's first video and even if it got written out of reality I fucking remember the music video. The band had been intentionally hiding info, even just dripping out pieces of names... not a face anywhere. Then early April it hit, BAM! The video for "A Drowning" was a collection of polaroids, some taken before a wedding... others from a crime scene after the wedding showing the bodies. It was the first time we saw Trent's new wife and lead singer of HtDA, Mariqueen Maandig, if only in these photos. We wouldn't know who was holding these photos and tossing them around the crime scene until the next video, the sequel... "The Space in Between" would finally show it all in video form, not just photos.

I remember the polaroids especially. I love Polaroid cameras and physical film. I remember feeling so happy to hear the difference in this new sound and how they'd brought it together. Actually it had to be late April. What happened that got the video erased? Was it Deep Water Horizon and all the US reporters thrown in jail? WikiLeaks? Shit... I'm not digging through internet searches to see what "the big thing" was that they rewrote, but it's always pieces of beauty like this that take stray bullets just so they can steer the simulation towards the next level... in the never-ending fucking war to outrun entropy.

Yeah, sure.. . The Wyrm loses another round. But what did _we_ lose to take that victory? Sometimes I wish I didn't remember. _But fuck that shit!_ Someone has to remember the victims.

## Download + Extended Listening

My remix of "A Drowning" is available for free download ([Bandcamp](https://sanjayaprime.bandcamp.com/album/remixes-and-mashups)). If you like this remix, I've also got my mashup "[The Making of a Violent Cyborg Heart](making-of-a-violent-cyborg-heart)" in the same collection, as well as my remix of "Discipline" by NIN. Then with the popularity of the remix, I made a second cut of the song (without any HtDA samples) for my "[Last Memory of Laughter](other-original-music)" EP, the song "Underwater Grave \[Drowned\]" ([Bandcamp](https://sanjayaprime.bandcamp.com/album/the-last-memory-of-laughter)). LiLi Glitch was one of my biggest fans for my remix of "A Drowning" and the moment she realized what she was hearing in "Underwater Grave" her eyes lit up and grew so big... I'll never forget that moment. _Priceless!_
